statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail steps down to 19, back into the low band, because the US cash session has now closed with a fully resolved two-way path: the Nasdaq-100 gapped up, sold through its prior close, defended 30,235.67 and recovered into a green finish. Stress eases one point to 71 as WTI falls 3.83% while the 30-year yield holds near a 24-year high.
recommendation: Tail at 19 sits below the watch threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON with a green status. The only elevated-band window on the published horizon is the 13:00 UTC hour on 30 September, where post-PCE repricing overlaps the US cash open; conditional Tail peaks at 25 there and the published danger window spans 12:00 to 15:00 UTC to cover the ADP, core PCE and GDP block, the cash open, Chicago PMI and EIA crude stocks. Every other forecast hour stays in the low or watch band. The mapping is derived from Tail alone; Stress remains high at 71 and does not affect the action.
headline: Cash NDX closed 30,339.33, up 0.21%, reclaiming 103.66 points from a 30,235.67 low inside a 0.64% range; VIX 16.05 and WTI down 3.83% to 89.02 pull Tail to 19, while a 5.62% 30-year yield keeps Stress high
body: The clearest current evidence is the completed US cash session. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 30,339.33, up 62.52 points or 0.21%. It opened at 30,412.29 above the 30,276.81 prior close, printed a 30,429.97 high, sold through that prior close to a 30,235.67 low, then recovered 103.66 points to finish green. The 194.30-point range is 0.64% of index level and, critically, retracements worked in both directions: the upside gap was retraced and the downside probe was retraced in turn. That is the structural opposite of the persistent no-retracement path the Tail score is designed to measure, which is why Tail returns to the low band at 19 even though the macro backdrop remains difficult. NQ futures corroborate the read at 30,630.75, up 0.21%, inside a 30,372.25 to 30,725.50 range. Volatility is contained: VIX closed 16.05, down 0.12%, near the 15.73 low of a 15.73 to 16.44 range. The Stress score stays high at 71 for reasons that are macro rather than price-path. The 30-year Treasury yield touched 5.62%, its highest since 2002, and the 10-year sits at 5.26%, with roughly 70% market-implied odds of a Federal Reserve rate increase in October. Conference Board consumer confidence fell 6.7 points to 81.9, the lowest since 2014, with 12-month inflation expectations at 6.1% and JOLTS job openings easing to 7.097 million. Against that, WTI fell 3.83% to 89.02 and Brent to roughly 96 as Saudi export flows recovered, which marginally relieves the energy-driven inflation impulse behind the long-end move. Megacap participation was split four to four on the latest session, with Meta up 2.65% and Broadcom up 1.66% offsetting Apple down 2.59% and Tesla down 1.28%; the chip complex was similarly mixed, ARM up 4.05% against Qualcomm down 1.26%. Shared Finviz context was read and reported collectionStatus partial, with its futures section unavailable and its calendar section unavailable; breadth, megacap, semiconductor and earnings sections were used only as delayed latest-session confirmation and carry no source as-of timestamp, so none of it was treated as live NQ price-path evidence. The forward picture is dominated by one window. ADP prints at 12:15 UTC on 30 September and the core PCE, headline PCE and final Q2 GDP block follows at 12:30 UTC, with forecasters having raised the August core PCE call toward 0.3% month over month, and the US cash open follows at 13:30 UTC. That single 13:00 UTC hour stacks a credible delayed-second-leg mechanism, where a bond-market reaction feeds a later equity leg, with opening-auction continuation risk, against a long end already at multi-decade highs. Conditional Tail reaches 25 there and nowhere else on the horizon. Consistent with the risk contract, the surrounding release hours are held at the watch ceiling rather than pushed into the elevated band, because event importance and forecast dispersion inform Stress and Confidence until an actual price path is observed.

lookbackSummary: 23 of the 24 preceding hours carry a published Claude assessment; the 14:00 UTC slot on 29 September is unavailable because no assessment was published in that clock hour. Tail ranged from 17 to 24 and never entered the elevated band. It troughed at 17 through the late Monday and early Tuesday overnight, printed 24 in the 01:00, 03:00, 04:00 and 15:00 UTC hours on trend-down readings, and settled at 20 to 21 across the US cash session. Stress declined steadily from 79 in the early European hours to 72 by 19:00 UTC as volatility decayed, while Confidence held between 86 and 88 throughout. The dominant mode was mixed for most of the window, with trend-down episodes overnight and around the 15:00 UTC hour and a single trend-up reading at 12:00 UTC.
outlookSummary: The published forecast opens at Tail 19 for the current post-close hour, where the resolved two-way cash path is actually observed, then eases to a horizon low of 18 across the US evening and the first Asian hours. It rebuilds gradually to 19 through late Asia and enters the watch band at 20 with the European pre-open, peaking at 21 around the European cash open. The pre-release build carries Tail to 22 in the 11:00 UTC hour and 24 for the 12:00 UTC ADP, core PCE and GDP release hour. The single elevated-band slot is 13:00 UTC, at Tail 25 and a mapped BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES state, because post-release repricing overlaps the 13:30 UTC cash open against a long end at multi-decade highs. Tail then decays to 23, 22 and 21 across the US morning and returns to the 20 watch floor in the afternoon, ticking to 21 for the closing hour where Micron reports after the bell. Stress tracks a similar shape between 69 and 79 and never leaves the high band, while Confidence decays from 88 to 82 into the release hours before recovering to 85 as live evidence is restored. Every forecast value beyond the current hour is conditional risk, not observed structure.
